# Serving live data

Read when the service exposes SSE or WebSocket streams.

- Choose SSE for one-way HTTP streaming and WebSocket for a genuinely bidirectional session; polling
  may be simpler for low-frequency state. Confirm proxy and platform timeout/buffering behavior.
- Native browser `EventSource` cannot attach an `Authorization` header. Prefer an approved
  same-origin HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite session with origin/CSRF controls or mint a short-lived,
  read-only, stream-specific credential. Never put the primary access token in the URL.
- For SSE, emit event IDs, honor `Last-Event-ID`, define replay retention and duplicate handling,
  send bounded retry guidance/keepalives, and disable buffering only where the deployed proxy requires.
- Bound concurrent streams, per-client buffers, event size/rate, and reconnect attempts. Drop or
  disconnect slow consumers instead of accumulating unbounded memory.
- Define terminal authentication failure, logout/revocation, shutdown draining, heartbeat/idle close,
  and client cleanup. Measure open streams, disconnect reasons, lag, dropped events, and replay.
